copilot-pull-request-reviewer re-reviewed the round-4 fix commit and raised 2 NEW in-scope findings on the sweep-eval/aggregate path (same regression class as the original threads: Floor-2 misclassification + a fan-in trust-boundary hole). Both FIXED (rule #12). (1) deriveRunFacts applies Floor-1 safe-room active-time credit unconditionally, but sweep-eval accepts --floor and would score a Floor-2 batch with Floor-1 win semantics. The tool is Floor-1-calibrated by construction (budgetMs is always FLOOR1_TIME_BUDGET_MS; no Floor-2 budget exists), so threading floorId into deriveRunFacts would be uncalibrated. Instead enforce the Floor-1 precondition at BOTH boundaries: sweep-eval parseArgs now throws on --floor != floor1; ShardMeta gains a floorId field (written by buildMeta); mergeShards rejects a non-floor1 first-shard meta AND a cross-shard floorId mismatch; deriveRunFacts docstring documents the precondition. (2) the schema-version guard proves safeRoomMs is EXPECTED at v2 but not that a row HAS a sane value — an omitted field (activeTimeMs ?? 0) silently restores raw-time classification, a value > gameTimeMs clamps active time to 0 (manufacturing an official win for any victory), and NaN misclassifies as a loss. Added assertRowSafeRoomInRange validating finite gameTimeMs>=0 and finite safeRoomMs in [0, gameTimeMs], called at the mergeShards row-loop fan-in boundary. Tests: all-floor2-batch rejection + a safeRoomMs domain it.each (missing/NaN/negative/over-gameTimeMs). verify:fast green; aggregate-shards unit test 36/36.

copilot-pull-request-reviewer re-reviewed the round-5 fix commit (c8372d08) and raised 1 finding on scoring.ts:122: the strict `<` budget comparison could misclassify an exact-budget run because gameTimeMs is ACCUMULATED (repeated += GAME.DELTA_MS, simulation-step.ts:120) while safeRoomMs is a MULTIPLICATION (safeRoomFrames * GAME.DELTA_MS, headless-runner.ts), so activeTimeMs = gameTimeMs - safeRoomMs carries FP drift; the reviewer claimed the 21_600-frame boundary could represent slightly BELOW 360_000 and count an exact-budget run as a win, and asked to cover the case with a value accumulated from GAME.DELTA_MS. INVESTIGATED (numerical experiment in Node, faithful to the real runner which always steps GAME.DELTA_MS): 1000/60 = 16.666666666666668 rounds UP in IEEE-754, so repeated addition drifts UPWARD -> accumulate(21_600) = 360000.00000005 (ABOVE budget) -> `< 360000` = false = correctly a loss (matches the game's `elapsed >= deadline` timeout). Every mixed accumulate-minus-multiply case with 21_600 active frames also landed active > 360_000 -> correctly a loss; 21_599 frames = 359983.33 -> a win. The drift magnitude (~5e-8 ms) is ~8 orders of magnitude below the 16.67 ms frame quantum, so it can NEVER flip an adjacent-frame classification, and 360_000/(1000/60) = 21_600 is an EXACT integer so the budget maps to a real boundary frame. The reviewer's suggested `< budget + epsilon` tolerance would INTRODUCE a bug (flip the exact-budget run to a win, contradicting the timeout semantics). ADJUDICATION (rule #12 - fix the test/gate around the requirement, never the requirement around a review): production code is provably correct -> NO scoring.ts change; instead LOCKED the boundary with a test-only regression suite in scoring-official-win.test.ts that mirrors the runner's accumulation + multiplication forms and asserts exact-budget = loss / one-frame-under = win / accumulate-minus-multiply boundary correct (commit 439755fe). Directly answers the reviewer's 'cover the case using a value accumulated from GAME.DELTA_MS' ask and protects the boundary against a future DELTA_MS change. verify:fast green; scoring-official-win 16/16.

copilot-pull-request-reviewer re-reviewed HEAD 1d91f62a (the frame-cap fix commit) and raised 2 findings; both addressed per rule #12. (1) [winrate-sweep-args.ts] The Floor-1 DEFAULT_MAX_FRAMES slack cap (23,760) was assigned to the maxFrames default for EVERY floor at object construction, BEFORE --floor was parsed, so a `--floor floor2` sweep without an explicit --max-frames silently jumped from the prior BUDGET_FRAMES (21,600) default to 23,760 -- an out-of-scope behavior change that could flip formerly-truncated floor2 runs to victories. ADDRESSED (correct structural fix, not resolve-to-green): added a maxFramesProvided flag + a post-parse floor-aware override so the slack cap is applied ONLY on floor1; any other floor retains the prior BUDGET_FRAMES default; an explicit --max-frames still overrides for every floor. Added a regression test (floor1/default -> 23,760; floor2/floor3 -> 21,600; explicit --max-frames honored on any floor). (2) [handoff .md] The durable handoff called the PR metric-only / no runner-behavior change and said winrate-sweep kept its 360s cap with no maxFrames change, but the shipped code raised the Floor-1 default 21,600 -> 23,760 (396s). ADDRESSED: corrected the title, summary, and scope section to state the Floor-1 cap was ALIGNED to the shared slack budget (23,760/396s, byte-identical to sweep-eval.ts + the ab-*/headless peer harnesses) as a correctness requirement (a safe-room-credited win can finish past 360s raw and would otherwise be truncated before isOfficialWin classifies it), while only inflation BEYOND that shared cap was rejected. verify:fast green; winrate-sweep-args 29/29.

Every peer Floor-1 harness (sweep-eval.ts IN THIS PR, the floor1-completion official gate, the ab-* and navmesh sweeps) uses the ~1.1x slack cap 23_760 (396s). Adjudicator (claude-opus-4.8): VALID -- an incomplete-migration defect inside the PR's own scope. FIXED: winrate-sweep-args.ts now exports DEFAULT_MAX_FRAMES = Math.ceil((FLOOR1_TIME_BUDGET_MS * 1.1) / GAME.DELTA_MS) (= 23_760, byte-identical to peers via the FP-safe division form; Math.ceil(BUDGET_FRAMES*1.1) would give 23_761), the default args use it, plus a regression test pinning 23_760 and > BUDGET_FRAMES. This ALSO reconciles the stale round-3 note: code_review round-4 changed the fail-record builder from outcome!==victory to !officialWin, so the round-3 'fail-record correctly left as outcome!==victory' claim is SUPERSEDED -- current code builds the fail record on !officialWin. clean:false pending a confirming round.

Confirming round on the applied frame-cap fix; 2 distinct models. gpt-5.4 (re-review of the fix): confirmed it matches peers (23_760, regression test locks it) but raised a RESIDUAL -- a 396s RAW cap still cannot GUARANTEE observability of a win with >36s safe-room dwell whose active time is near budget (could finish >396s raw); suggested further cap inflation / an active-frame cap. Independently adjudicated by claude-sonnet-4.6 (2nd distinct model): residual is OUT-OF-SCOPE and the fix is terminal. Decisive load-bearing argument (gate consistency): winrate-sweep now uses the IDENTICAL 23_760-frame cap as the OFFICIAL Floor-1 gate (floor1-completion.test.ts) and every peer sweep; isOfficialWin requires outcome===victory first, so a run truncated past 23_760 frames can be an official win in NEITHER the sweep NOR the gate -- they observe/miss exactly the same set. INFLATING the sweep cap beyond the gate would let the sweep count a win the gate force-terminates as a timeout -> the sweep would report a HIGHER win-rate than the gate validates = a NEW divergence, the opposite of the SSOT alignment this PR enforces. The 23_760-frame cap IS the definition of the observable Floor-1 window; a win outside it is, by design, not a win the system can validate. Corroborating (not decisive): empirically every over-budget safe-room victory completed within 396s (plan review + maintainer); and the active-frame-cap alternative was a plan-review option the maintainer DECLINED as out-of-metric-only-scope, so reversing it silently would violate rule #12. valid_count=0 (the residual is out-of-scope, not a defect). TERMINAL CLEAN: 2 distinct models, no valid unresolved concern on the final head.
